projects.title: An Academic Study Comparing WebRTC and LLHLS Streaming Protocols
projects.description: My 3rd year dissertation proposal project covering the research and development of a seminar hosting platform and the testing of two streaming technologies.
projects.information: This project is my 3rd year dissertation project, covering the proposal before the implementation. This module is designed for us to plan, analyse, and prepare for the dissertation. The reason I chose this topic is because of the interesting recent developments with streaming technologies such as Apple introducing Low-Latency HLS, a more real-time optimised version of HLS. From analysing literature and previous works, among the streaming technologies LLHLS and WebRTC are commonly seen to be the most optimised and fastest streaming technologies, however, each has a different specialty; WebRTC for few-to-few and LLHLS for one-to-many. The end result from this paper should provide valuable research into the theory of dynamic protocol switching; switching between LLHLS and WebRTC based on client numbers. The paper covers an in-depth literature review, proposed methodology, research philosophy, and an analysis of expected results. The data analysis section of the paper utilises G*Power, hypothesis testing, ANOVA analysis, tukey testing, and the outputting of graphs all completed in R.

projects.title: Evaluating WebSocket Performance against Geographic Distance
projects.description: A performance analysis of the effect of geographical distance on WebSockets using a JavaScript client-server setup to evaluate latency and throughput using a VPN with varying packet sizes, analysing the results in R.
projects.information: This project evaluates and measures the effect geographical distance has on WebSocket performance. The inspiration behind this project was to investigate the latency experienced by long-distance communication and if it had any correlation to the geographical distance between them. This project uses NordVPN to simulate a client being present within a different country, sending text packets across to a server and retrieving them, calculating the Round Trip Time (RTT). Once recorded, the data was analysed in R and generated into graphs.

projects.title: Re-Space
projects.description: A plant enivronment monitor comprised of a developed API, hardware system, react native application, and a dockerised server.
projects.information: This project is a multi-component system that works as a proof-of-concept for a plant environment monitoring system. This project outlines the process for implementing a miniature greenhouse that can monitor plants and their environment, improving their lifespan. Currently this system works as a plant pot monitor, which monitors lighting, temperature, and moisture, sending these values to a dockerised API and then to a mobile application that the user can download.

projects.title: AI Face Detection Performance Analysis
projects.description: An academic analysis of the performance of AI Face Detection algorithms.
projects.information: This project was a comparison of five face detection algorithms against the effects of lighting quality. This project was implemented in Python using five different libraries for face detection. To test these algorithms, a dataset was used with each subject exposed to three lighting angles: left, right, and central, then these images were dimmed or brightened for a more accurate test.

projects.title: Halwill Baptist Church Website
projects.description: A project designed for a local church based on my portfolio website.
projects.information: This project is a free uncommissioned request from my GrandFathers church, tasked with creating an informative and friendly website for the church. The system is designed to be as friendly as possible, with clear buttons and tabs with informative names. The website features a front-end admin login, requiring username and password for authorisation. This system is salted, peppered, hashed, and encrypted, providing very strong security. However, this will be improved on in the future, applying DDoS prevention. The admin page allows the church admin to edit and add new events or news, updating, deleting, and archiving as needed. The admin can upload pictures, links, locations and information to provide as much detail as possible. Unfortunately the website is missing the content which has been requested multiple times but has not been provided. The website is not currently live but on receiving and updating the content it will be.

projects.title: Cormoran
projects.description: Cormoran: a video game I helped develop in Unity.
projects.information: Cormoran is the title of one of the video games I helped produce in my first year of university. In GAM190, the name given to this module, we as a team were tasked with creating a video game with the constraint: Local history. Cormoran is a game based on the legend of Jack the Giant Slayer, a Cornish legend turned global. The premise for this game is that the player (Jack) needs to find a way to kill Cormoran, seeking revenge for his father. The player navigates around St Micheals Mount, locating objects and eventually digging a hole for Cormoran to fall into, all while avoiding him. For this project, I was the developer behind the AI for the giant. This included navMesh pathfinding, raycasting, waypoint management, and player tracking. This was a very enjoyable game to work on and I would love to continue with it at some point later on.

projects.title: Delivery Drone Robot Education Simulation
projects.description: An educational simulation for Delivery Drones paired with a hand-made controller.
projects.information: This was one of my first year projects. I was tasked with integrating an Arduino system into Unity, and creating an educational piece of software that works alongside a custom built controller. For this project, I based my idea off of the company Zipline and their delivery drones. My Controller was a gyroscopic input that reacted to 2 axes of rotation. Up and down rotation affects the falling speed of the delivery, while left and right affects the position of the delivery. As the user progresses through the story, text popups appear, explaining the process and benefits. The user was challenged with placing the delivery on a cross outside the recipients door.
